item.text: Victoria’s Royal Commission into the Management of Police Informants examined police use of a defence barrister as an informant and how criminal cases might have been affected.
item.support: The number of, and extent to which, cases may have been affected

item.text: It also examined safeguards for informants with confidentiality obligations, disclosure to prosecutors and courts, and reforms to prevent similar conduct.
item.support: the use of information from such sources in criminal proceedings

item.text: The Commission concluded that convictions or findings of guilt involving 1,011 people may have been affected by police use of the barrister.
item.support:

item.text: It identified failures in leadership, governance, supervision, training and risk management that allowed the conduct to continue.
item.section: Victoria Police’s conduct: systemic issues and causal factors
item.support:
These include failures 
of leadership and governance, of management and supervision, of policy and training

item.text: Its 111 recommendations cover further investigation, disclosure to affected people, informant management, independent oversight and implementation monitoring.
item.support: The Commission has made 111 recommendations, as listed below.

item.quote:
After a rigorous analysis of the evidence, including all relevant submissions, the Commission has concluded that 
the convictions or findings of guilt of 1,011 people may have been affected by Victoria Police’s use of Ms Gobbo 
as a human source.
The conduct of some officers fell well short of an acceptable standard.
